text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The director of monopoly gas distributor SPP s.p., Arpad Demko, was dismissed and relaced by former Economics Minister Jan Ducky, who is also a current deputy for the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia.
- It is widely believed that Demko was dismissed for his critical attitude toward a planned contract between SPP and the Russian company Gazprom.

- President Michal Kovac on Tuesday strictly dismissed Prime Minister Vladmir Meciar's statements that a U.S.-Russian treaty on NATO enlargement excluded Slovakia from the first wave of new members. Kovac said Slovakia's future will be determined by its ability to show democratic principles respected in NATO countries.
- Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik is Slovakia's candidate for chairman of the United Nations's 52nd General Assembly.

- Independent economists oppose a government draft on the so-called revitalisation of the industry, saying the law violates free market competition rules and that it can damage competitiveness abroad.
- Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar on Wednesday begins a two-day official visit to Turkey.

- Judges of the International Court of Justice on Tuesday began a two-day inspection of the Slovak part of the controversial Gabcikovo dam on the Danube river, currently the subject of a dispute being fought out between Hungary and Slovakia at the U.N. court.

- Slovakia's sole tyre producer Matador Puchov said its Russian joint-venture Matador Omskshina was less effective than expected and that it has had financial problems resulting from the insolvency of the Russian market.

- Slovakia's industrial production should rise month- on-month in March, according to a survey by the Slovak Statistical Bureau among producers accounting for about 59 percent of the country's overall industrial output.

- Minority shareholders of Slovakia's largest confectioner, Jacobs Suchard Figaro a.s., are demanding an extraordinary shareholders meeting to dismiss management and the supervisory board for alleged violation of minority shareholder rights.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Slovak Entrepeneur Union has threatened to postpone contributions to all state funds, totalling some 378 million crowns a month, if it does not recieve a response to its demand for a dialogue with Meciar over the current problems in the economy.
- The state-owned postal monopoly, Slovenska Posta s.p. raised tarrifs for its services by an average 20 percent on April 1.

SME - The U.S. embassy to Slovakia has strictly rejected Meciar's statement about an alleged treaty between Washington and Moscow on NATO enlargement, which should exlude Slovakia from the first wave of new NATO members.

- Meciar has accused President Kovac of attempting to de-stabilise the government by rejecting his request for dismissal of Transport Minister Alexander Rezes. Last month Kovac rejected the request, saying it was in contradiction to the constitution.
